messages:
Sam: heads up — deploybot just flagged a p95 regression on embeddings-service after the v2.5.0 rollout (northamerica-prod). auto-action suggested: route traffic to v2-legacy or rollback. I need quick ops decision, pinging @Nina and @Leo.
deploy-bot: DEPLOYBOT NOTICE — metric p95_latency increased 32% over baseline in last 5m. Suggested mitigations: 1) route 100% to model=v2-legacy for 15m 2) manual rollback to v2.4.8. Confidence=high. Links: https://telemetry/redwood/embeddings/p95
Priya: confirmed, seeing ~18% malformed responses in the sampled generation logs. kvcache misses spike when sequence length > 1024 on the new quantized kernels. Not an immediate crash but quality regression for some client prompts.
Leo: quick context — v2.5.0 swapped in new kernel set + eager kvcache flush. If we rollback to 2.4.8 it's a straightforward pin but we'll lose the quant perf gains. Rolling back is ~2m to flip and verify, but it will impact dedicated pools if any customers are pinned to 2.5.0.
Priya: agree. Is there a cheap temporary option? Can we route to v2-legacy for just the problematic region/route?
Leo: yes. My recommendation: do a traffic-slice to v2-legacy for northamerica-prod 100% for 15m while we validate fixes. Command (ops):

```sh
redwood route set --service embeddings-service --region northamerica-prod --model v2-legacy --percent 100 --duration 15m --reason "p95 regression auto-fallback"
```

This preserves the release history and avoids touching dedicated pins.
Nina: from a comms POV — if we keep the release and route to legacy temporarily, we should still update the release notes with an interim note and add a banner for affected customers. If we fully rollback, we need a short customer email and a support playbook.
Sam: I can draft the release note blurb and the support snippet. Draft: "We observed a quality regression for long-context embeddings in v2.5.0 for a subset of requests. We're routing affected traffic to v2-legacy while we investigate; no customer action required."
ops-runner: ops-check — do we have approval to run the route command? Who signs off on a manual rollback if we choose that route?
Leo: for routing it's ops + oncall approval. For full rollback we need product + eng-release signoff (Nina + Sam) + ops to execute.
Nina: I approve routing to legacy as a mitigant. Will reserve rollback decision until we have 15m telemetry. Sam please send the release blurb to #customer-comms draft channel.
Sam: sending now. /me posts draft to #customer-comms
ops-runner: executing routing command now.
deploy-bot: ACTION LOG — routing change requested by ops-runner. Executing route set to model=v2-legacy for northamerica-prod (100% for 15m). Rollback flag: false. Run ID: rb-3187654321-01
ops-runner: done — route applied. watching metrics.
Priya: initial telemetry looks better within 90s, malformed responses down to 2.1% from 18%.
Leo: nice. leaving the traffic-slice in place for the 15m window. we'll capture traces and kvcache stats and open a postmortem if needed.
Nina: publishing short note to customers and adding banner to console: "Scoped mitigation applied for embeddings v2.5.0; routing traffic to v2-legacy. Investigating; ETA 2 hours." Copy in #customer-comms.
Sam: thanks all. action items: (1) eng-ml to root-cause the kvcache/regression (Priya + Leo), (2) Sam/Nina to finalize comms, (3) ops to leave routing until we see stable metrics or decide to rollback. I'll create a checklist ticket.
Priya: started a debug run and reproducer. I'll update thread in 10m with findings.
ops-runner: marking run rb-3187654321-01 as live. ping me for a manual rollback runbook if we need it. :thumbsup:
Sam: closing loop for now. thanks everyone. :pray:
